attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Medical cover for the Harbour Harriers Heritage Run 10K, Sunday 7 March 2027

From Daniel Mwangi, Event Secretary, Harbour Harriers Athletic Club

The race is a 10K with 180 runners and starts at 10:00. An ambulance from Halden Medical Transport is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

First aid
We'll have 3 first aid posts, at the start, the finish and halfway, with 8 trained first aiders between them, so nobody on the course is more than about a kilometre and a half from help. We also have two first aiders on bikes, carrying defibrillators.

Runners get an email in race week telling them to dress for the weather and to keep a phone with them if they can. Most have run with us before. The list of entrants includes an emergency contact for each runner, which is kept at the start.

Heat, cold and water
We always tell runners to dress sensibly for the weather and to keep drinking, and it's all in the email we send them the week before. We'll be watching the forecast, and people here are used to all sorts of weather.

If someone needs hospital
The nearest emergency department is at Valley Regional Hospital, 16 km from the finish. We've walked the route out from the pick-up point at the top of Quay Street with the first aiders, and we've told the hospital the date and how many are coming.

Staying in touch
We'll all have our phones, and I'll send a list of numbers round the team the week before. The signal is usually fine around there.

Who's responsible
Our medical lead is Samuel Adeyemi, a registered paramedic, who'll be there from an hour before the start until the last runner is in and has the final word on pulling any runner out.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Harbour Harriers Heritage Run 10K: how the race will work

Prepared by Daniel Mwangi (Event Secretary), Harbour Harriers Athletic Club. Last updated 11 October 2026.

This is our plan for race day, Sunday 7 March 2027. We expect 180 runners over 10K (10 km). Numbers can be collected from the top of Quay Street from an hour before we go at 10:00, and we aim to have the last finisher home by 12:00.

The route takes in Quay Street, Ash Avenue and Dyer Street, and the City would need to close all of these for us. On the way round we cross Queen's Road, Victoria Road, Dock Road and Cross Avenue. We finish in Ferry Park lawn.

It's a lovely route through the old part of town, though there isn't much room. We measured Quay Street at 5.5 metres and Dyer Street at 3.5 metres, doorstep to doorstep. Two cars can't pass on Ash Avenue. People watching tend to stand in doorways.

Our club has put on races for some years now and we keep to the same simple format: chip timing, water on the course, and a hot drink at the end. Results go up on our website the same evening.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Traffic arrangements for the Harbour Harriers Heritage Run 10K, Sunday 7 March 2027

From Daniel Mwangi, Event Secretary, Harbour Harriers Athletic Club

We have tried to think through what happens on the roads on race day. The race is a 10K, it starts at 10:00, and it goes through the Foundry Yards area. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

Closing the roads
The big one is Quay Street, which we would like closed from about 08:30. For the rest of the route we've found in past years that cars are few at that time of the morning, and our marshals are very good at slowing them down as the runners come through.

Crossings
Where we cross a major road we will have people stationed from 08:30 until the last runner is through. At Queen's Road, where it meets Quay Street, there will be 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Victoria Road, where it meets Quay Street, there will be 3 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Dock Road, where it meets Dyer Street, there will be 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Cross Avenue, where it meets Ash Avenue, there will be 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor.

Getting around the closures
We've worked out the way round for drivers and Northline Barriers will sign it. Traffic off Quay Street goes via Church Road and Ferry Road, signed from Abbey Road. Traffic off Ash Avenue goes via Prince Street and Station Road, signed from Garrison Street. Traffic off Dyer Street goes via Canal Road and Ferry Road, signed from Weir Street.

Some background. Our committee has run races in this part of Port Halden for a number of years, and most of our members live locally. The council's traffic controller looked over an early sketch of the route last year, though not this version of the plan.

Emergency vehicles
I've no doubt an ambulance or a fire engine would get through if one were needed. Everybody on our team knows to get out of the way and to help in any way they can, and we'll be sure to mention the race to the fire station.

Letting people know
Every house and shop on the closed streets gets a letter three weeks before and a reminder a week before. We'll put up the yellow notice boards ten days ahead, and we've told the bus company the times.

Afterwards
Once it's all over the team will collect the cones and barriers, and everyone can get back to normal.
